STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of mashed potatoes with gravy and a sliced dark brown meat (looks like a sausage/meatloaf or similar link cut into slices, laid flat). Photo taken from above, slightly angled; the plate is a white rectangular-rounded dish.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White plate roughly 26 cm across in its long dimension; estimated usable width of the plate about 22 cm, so area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2 for the circular-equivalent footprint. Food covers the central/right portion.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) mashed potatoes with gravy poured over, (b) sliced dark brown meat (sausage/meatloaf-like) on the left side.

STEP 4 - Area: Mashed potatoes ~50% of plate area (~190 cm^2). Meat slices ~10% (~38 cm^2). Gravy is spread over the potatoes, so it is counted within the potato area, with a small share of ~3% (~11 cm^2) assigned separately as a sauce layer on top.

STEP 5 - Volume: Mashed potatoes 190 cm^2 x 3 cm ≈ 570 ml (outer envelope, pile is mounded). Meat slices 38 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 46 ml. Gravy 11 cm^2 x 0.4 cm ≈ 4 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Mashed potatoes 570 ml x 0.9 ≈ 513 g (dense mashed item). Meat 46 ml x 0.95 ≈ 44 g. Gravy 4 ml x 1.0 ≈ 4 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Mashed potatoes (made with butter/milk) ~110 kcal/100 g: 513 g → ~565 kcal. Meat slices (sausage/meatloaf-type, cooked) ~250 kcal/100 g: 44 g → ~110 kcal. Gravy ~60 kcal/100 g: 4 g → ~2 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A mounded side of mashed potatoes plus a few slices of meat on a large plate is plausible at roughly 560 g total, about 680 kcal. The potato estimate is the largest uncertainty; it may be somewhat smaller if the mound is flatter.

Total ≈ 561 g, ≈ 677 kcal.
